title: Crop Insurance Member Terms: Schedule of Unpaid Premium Figures
content:
The figures that govern Crop Insurance premium, fees and interest left unpaid are the same at every plan and coverage level.

| Plan and coverage level | Interest-free period after the billing date | Simple interest per month or part of a month | Termination date (year after the crop year) | Ineligibility on termination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |
| Revenue Protection 65% Coverage | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |
| Revenue Protection 70% Coverage | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |
| Revenue Protection 75% Coverage | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |
| Revenue Protection 80% Coverage | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |
| Revenue Protection 85% Coverage | 30 calendar days | 1.25% | March 15 | Yes |

Notes to the schedule:

1. *Interest-free period* — Calendar days after the billing date after which unpaid premium accrues interest.
2. *Simple interest* — Simple interest per month (or part of a month) on unpaid premium, %.
3. *Termination date* — Month-day of the year after the crop year on which a policy with unpaid premium is terminated for indebtedness.
4. *Ineligibility on termination* — whether a policy terminated for indebtedness makes the member ineligible for federal crop insurance until the debt is paid.

Illustrations on hypothetical figures:

- Interest is simple, so each month or part of a month carries the same charge: on an illustrative $2,000.00 left unpaid, one month or part of a month at 1.25% is $25.00, and three months or parts of months are $75.00.
- The termination date falls in the year after the crop year: for a hypothetical 2025 crop year it is March 15, 2026.
- Because ineligibility on termination is Yes at every level, a termination for indebtedness at any level makes the member ineligible for federal crop insurance until the debt is paid.
